methodological_rigor.justification: Single-institution retrospective study of 15 patients with recurrent/metastatic gynecological malignancies treated with MR-Linac adaptive SBRT; October 2019-May 2025 timeframe. Primary endpoints (OS, PFS, LC) appropriately defined; Kaplan-Meier analysis appropriate for survival estimation. However, very small sample size (n=15) limits power for statistical comparisons; median follow-up only 4.67 months insufficient for long-term outcome assessment. No control arm or propensity matching; treatment decisions not randomized.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Feasibility/pilot study demonstrating MR-Linac adaptive SBRT combined with systemic therapy achieves 73.3% ORR and 92.3% six-month local control in challenging patient population (recurrent/metastatic gynecological cancers). Direct clinical relevance for treatment-refractory disease, but lacks comparison with standard palliative approaches or observation to establish incremental benefit.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods transparently described including patient selection, MR-Linac workflow, dose constraints (AAPM TG-101, ESTRO-EORTC consensus), and outcome metrics. However, lacks formal structured reporting standard adherence (HGSOC-RT, ASTRO guidelines not cited). Small sample limits interpretability; incomplete follow-up data (median 4.67 months). No pre-registration or data availability statement.

novelty_literature.justification: Applies established MR-Linac adaptive SBRT technology to relatively understudied indication (recurrent gynecological malignancies). Prior studies of adaptive SBRT exist; this work represents application-specific extension rather than methodological innovation. Combination with systemic therapy addresses known clinical gap but lacks mechanistic novelty.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with comprehensive introduction contextualizing clinical challenge of pelvic/abdominal re-irradiation. Methods detailed regarding dose prescriptions, constraints, and adaptive workflow. Results clearly presented with survival curves and response data. Limitations section appropriately acknowledges small sample size and short follow-up. Discussion compares favorably with historical data.

key_strengths: Addresses clinically important unmet need: safe treatment options for recurrent pelvic/abdominal gynecological cancers after prior therapy
High tumor response rate (73.3% ORR) with acceptable toxicity profile (1/15 dose-limiting enteric fistula) in heavily pretreated population
Demonstrates technical feasibility of adaptive MR-Linac SBRT with daily MRI-guided replanning; innovative 'see-treat-adapt' workflow
key_concerns: Very small sample (n=15) with heterogeneous histologies (cervical, endometrial, ovarian, vulvar); insufficient for meaningful statistical inference
Median follow-up 4.67 months (range 0.73-20 months) inadequate for late toxicity assessment or long-term survival conclusions
No comparative arm (standard palliative RT, chemotherapy, observation) limits ability to establish incremental benefit over alternatives
Lack of dose-response analysis or assessment of adaptation impact on outcomes (compare adaptive vs non-adaptive plans)
Heterogeneous systemic therapy regimens; unclear whether benefit attributable to SBRT or systemic treatment
chief_reviewer.rationale: Feasibility/pilot study demonstrating technical and clinical feasibility of MR-Linac adaptive SBRT in challenging gynecological cancer population with promising early outcomes. Appropriate for Tier 4 journals; minor revisions should include comparative analysis with historical controls and extended follow-up for late toxicity before wider adoption.
